title: Learned reconstruction reduces perfusion-measurement bias in shortened cardiac SPECT data
summary: A residual network reconstructed full-acquisition-like cardiac SPECT from reduced-count or reduced-projection data derived from 363 patient scans. Internal comparisons found closer perfusion-deficit measurements to the full acquisitions than the uncorrected shortened data. These are image-based clinical measurement results, without independently acquired short-scan validation, established diagnostic accuracy or demonstrated radiation-dose benefit.
ai_technology: Twenty-layer dilated residual convolutional neural networks for projection-domain SPECT reconstruction
organization: Geneva University Hospitals; University of Geneva; Sharif University of Technology; Iran University of Medical Sciences; Tehran University of Medical Sciences; University of Groningen; University of Southern Denmark

evidence.tested: A prospectively collected 363-person clinical cohort supplied full-acquisition list-mode data. Shorter-time data used the first half of acquisition events, while fewer-projection data omitted alternate views. Residual networks learned projection restoration; the source describes tenfold cross-validation on the cohort. Reconstructed clinical perfusion measures, including total perfusion deficit, were compared with full acquisitions using commercial quantitative software and agreement analyses. Learned reconstructions reduced measured bias relative to uncorrected reduced data.
evidence.unknown: Reduced acquisitions were derived from the same full scans, rather than separate real-world short scans. Full-acquisition reconstruction is a measurement reference, not independent disease truth. Detailed fold-specific preprocessing/tuning isolation is not established. Gated functional performance, diagnostic decisions, patient outcomes and actual lower-dose acquisition were not tested. Some headline image-metric labels and dispersion values are inconsistent, so they are not adopted as precise comparative claims.
evidence.ai_role: The learned residual networks restored projection information before reconstruction, enabling the represented within-cohort test of clinical perfusion-measurement agreement under reduced data.
